text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- OLACYR SAYS WILL RESIST PRESSURES
Itamarati group will not sell assets before reaching an agreement with its creditors, said the group's owner Olacyr de Moraes.
-- GARANTIA AND EVADIN TO BID FOR BAND B

Private bank Banco de Investimentos Garantia and electronics manufacturer group Evadin formed a consortium to bid for a concession to operate the so-called Band B cellular services. The international partner is Hutchison Telecommunications, a unit of Hong Kong's Hutchison Wampoa, which serves 2.3 million cellular users in ten countries.
-- TELEBRAS NETS 1.98 BLN REAIS

Telecommunications firm Telebras reported a net consolidated profit of 1.98 billion reais between January and September, while its holding company had a net profit of 2.389 billion reais. The firm's earnings rose 204 percent in real terms when compared with the same period of 1995.
-- TREASURY SHOWS 1.6 BLN REAL DEFICIT

The National Treasury showed a deficit of around 1.6 billion reais in October due to interest payments and a transfer of 500 million reais to states to cover losses with the elimination of the so-called ICMS tax.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- STATES RESIST SINGLE TAX

Brazilian states resist a new single tax for small firms created by the federal government. Small companies are now allowed to pay a single tax of between 5.0 percent and 7.5 percent. The tax will depend on the company's revenues.
-- TEN BABIES DIE IN RIO DE JANEIRO HOSPITAL IN 15 DAYS
Ten babies have died in the past 15 days at a hospital in Niteroi, Rio de Janeiro state. The most probable cause was a bacterial infection.
O GLOBO
-- CIVIL POLICE'S TOP GROUP INVESTIGATES STRAY BULLETS
Top officials at the Civil Police are investigating the cases of stray bullets in Rio de Janeiro city. On Wednesday, three more people were hurt by stray bullets.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom, 55-11-2485412
